Ligand 1 is the oxetane-cap molecule, the best QED of the active series at 0.905, held back only by SA 2.11; ligand 2 is its cyclobutyl twin, better SA but lower QED. Both carry a 4-methyl, which I now know costs about 0.04 of activity against a halogen. Atom 15 is the oxetane ring CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 13 over a non-ring bond, so anchoring there keeps the oxetane and lets me rebuild the rest. This is the second of the two combinations generation 2 implied but never built: the best-QED cap on a halogenated azine. Fluorine rather than chlorine, because it matched chlorine's 0.53 while being lighter and less lipophilic, and the oxetane is already pulling LogP down - so this is the most drug-like version of the active molecule I can assemble. The open question is whether the oxetane's SA penalty eats the QED gain, as it did on the para core. Expected product: about 287 Da.
